title: Buttered vegetables
intro: Corn, carrots and green beans blanched, then tossed in garlic butter with a pinch of sugar. Sweet, buttery and bright, the side that shows up next to fried chicken and grilled meats.

items.name: corn kernels
items.note: fresh, frozen or canned and drained

steps.text: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add the carrots and cook.
Add the green beans and cook until both are tender-crisp. Add the corn for the last minute.
Drain well and let the vegetables steam dry in the colander.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the garlic until fragrant, without letting it brown.
Add the vegetables and sugar and toss until glossy and hot. Season with salt and pepper and serve.

tips: A frozen mixed-vegetable bag of corn, carrots and peas works for a quick version: skip the blanching and toss it straight into the butter until hot.

title: Ginisang kabute
intro: Fresh mushrooms seared in butter with lots of garlic, then finished with soy sauce and a squeeze of calamansi. Meaty, salty and tangy, good with rice or as pulutan.

items.name: fresh mushrooms
items.note: button, shiitake or the gray wet-market kind, sliced or torn

steps.text: Heat the oil and half the butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and leave them alone until they brown underneath.
Toss and cook until the liquid they release has evaporated and they are browned all over.
Add the rest of the butter, the garlic, onion and chili, and cook until the garlic is fragrant.
Add the soy sauce and toss to coat. Turn off the heat and stir in the calamansi juice.
Season with pepper, sprinkle with green onions and serve.

tips: Do not salt the mushrooms early or crowd the pan; they will stew in their own water instead of browning.

title: Poqui-poqui
intro: Smoky grilled eggplant chopped and sautéed with garlic, onion and tomatoes, then scrambled with eggs. Soft, smoky and savory, eaten with rice.

steps.text: Grill the eggplants over charcoal or directly on a gas flame, turning, until the skin is charred all over and the flesh is completely soft.
Let them cool enough to handle, then peel off the skin and chop the flesh roughly.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic and onion until soft, then add the tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Add the eggplant and stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently until just set and still moist.
Taste, adjust the seasoning and serve with rice.

tips: Grilling over an open flame gives the smoky taste; a dry, hot cast-iron pan works too, just turn the eggplants often.

title: Pritong talong
intro: Long eggplants sliced and pan-fried until golden outside and creamy inside, served with a garlicky soy and vinegar dip. Plain, cheap and very satisfying with rice.

steps.text: Slice the eggplants diagonally about 1 cm thick. Sprinkle with the salt and let stand.
Pat the slices dry with paper towels.
Mix the dip ingredients in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry the eggplant in a single layer until golden on both sides and soft in the middle, working in batches.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with the dip.

tips: Salting first draws out water, so the eggplant browns better and soaks up less oil.

title: Tortang talong
intro: Grilled eggplants peeled, flattened into fans and fried in beaten egg. Smoky and soft inside a golden egg coat, eaten with rice and banana ketchup.

steps.text: Grill the eggplants over charcoal or a gas flame, turning, until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft all the way through.
Let them cool slightly, then peel off the skin, keeping the stem on. Lay each eggplant on a plate and flatten it gently with a fork.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper in a wide, shallow dish.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Dip one eggplant in the egg to coat both sides, lay it in the pan and spoon a little extra egg over it.
Fry until the egg is set and golden underneath, then flip and fry the other side. Repeat with the rest, adding oil as needed.
Serve hot with rice and banana ketchup.

tips: Leaving the stem on gives you a handle for dipping and flipping.

title: Tortang talong with giniling
intro: Flattened grilled eggplants topped with sautéed ground pork and fried in egg until golden. A heartier tortang talong that works as a full ulam.

steps.text: Grill the eggplants over charcoal or a gas flame, turning, until charred and completely soft.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic and onion until soft, add the pork and cook until browned, then add the tomato and soy sauce and cook until dry. Season with pepper and let cool.
Peel the eggplants, keeping the stems on, and flatten each on a plate with a fork.
Beat the eggs with the salt in a wide dish and stir in the cooled giniling.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Dip an eggplant in the egg, lay it in the pan and spoon some of the egg and pork over the top.
Fry until set and golden underneath, then flip carefully with a wide spatula and fry the other side. Repeat with the rest.
Serve hot with rice and banana ketchup.

tips: Cool the pork before mixing it with the egg, or it starts cooking the egg in the bowl.

title: Tortang giniling
intro: Ground pork sautéed with diced potato, onion and tomato, bound with egg and fried into thick golden patties. Savory, filling and good hot or at room temperature in a baon.

items.name: medium potato
items.note: peeled and cut into small dice

steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the potato until tender and lightly golden. Set aside.
In the same pan, cook the garlic and onion until soft. Add the pork and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Add the tomato and soy sauce and cook until the mixture is dry. Stir in the potato and let cool.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper in a bowl and stir in the cooled pork mixture.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Scoop in about 1/3 cup of the mixture per patty and flatten slightly. Fry until golden underneath, then flip and cook the other side.
Repeat with the rest, adding oil as needed. Serve with rice and banana ketchup.

tips: A tablespoon of raisins or a handful of green peas stirred into the filling is a common addition.

title: Tortang ampalaya
intro: Salted and squeezed bitter gourd slices set in a thick, flat omelet with onion and tomato. The egg mellows the bitterness, and it is eaten in wedges with rice.

steps.text: Halve the ampalaya lengthwise, scrape out the seeds and pith, and slice very thinly. Toss with the 2 teaspoons of salt and let stand.
Squeeze the slices hard, rinse in cold water and squeeze again until quite dry.
Heat the oil in a 25 cm nonstick pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and tomato until soft, add the ampalaya and toss until bright green.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper. Spread the vegetables evenly in the pan and pour the eggs over them.
Lower the heat, cover and cook until the bottom is golden and the top is almost set.
Slide the torta onto a plate, flip it back into the pan and cook the other side until set. Cut into wedges and serve.

tips: Slicing the ampalaya paper-thin and squeezing it well is what keeps the torta from tasting harsh.

title: Tortang alamang
intro: Fresh tiny alamang shrimp mixed with egg, flour and onion and fried into thin, crisp-edged patties. Briny and savory, best dipped in spiced vinegar.

items.name: fresh alamang (tiny shrimp)
items.note: not the fermented kind, rinsed and well drained

steps.text: Rinse the alamang in a fine sieve, picking out any debris, and let drain well.
Beat the eggs in a bowl, then stir in the flour, onion, green onions, salt and pepper until smooth. Fold in the alamang.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Drop in 2 tablespoons of batter per patty and spread thin with the back of the spoon.
Fry until golden and crisp at the edges, then flip and fry the other side.
Drain on paper towels and repeat with the rest. Serve hot with spiced vinegar.

tips: Fresh alamang is already salty from the sea, so fry one small test patty and adjust the salt before cooking the rest.

title: Tortang patatas
intro: Thin potato slices fried until tender with onion, then set in egg into a thick, golden potato omelet. Soft and savory, eaten in wedges with rice and ketchup.

items.name: medium potatoes
items.note: about 500 g, peeled and thinly sliced

steps.text: Heat the oil in a 25 cm nonstick pan over medium heat. Add the potatoes and cook, turning now and then, until tender but not browned.
Add the onion and cook until soft.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper. Spread the potatoes evenly in the pan and pour the eggs over.
Lower the heat, cover and cook until the bottom is golden and the top is nearly set.
Slide the torta onto a plate, flip it back into the pan and cook the other side until set.
Cut into wedges and serve warm with rice and ketchup.

tips: Pour off most of the oil before adding the eggs if the potatoes are swimming in it, leaving just enough to coat the pan.

title: Tortang kangkong
intro: Chopped water spinach leaves bound with egg and a little flour and fried into soft green patties. Mild and savory, a good way to use up a bunch of kangkong.

items.name: kangkong (water spinach)
items.note: leaves and tender tips only, about 1 bunch

steps.text: Blanch the kangkong in boiling water just until wilted, then drain, rinse in cold water and squeeze dry.
Chop the kangkong finely.
Beat the eggs in a bowl and whisk in the flour, salt and pepper. Stir in the kangkong, onion and garlic.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Spoon in about 3 tablespoons of the mixture per patty and flatten lightly.
Fry until golden underneath, then flip and fry the other side. Repeat with the rest.
Serve with rice and banana ketchup or vinegar.

tips: Squeeze the blanched kangkong really dry; extra water makes the patties fall apart in the pan.

title: Tortang corned beef
intro: Canned corned beef mixed with egg, onion and garlic and fried into crisp-edged patties. Salty, rich and a favorite for breakfast or baon.

steps.text: Break up the corned beef in a bowl with a fork. Add the eggs, onion, garlic, flour and pepper and mix well.
Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Scoop in about 1/4 cup of the mixture per patty and flatten slightly.
Fry until browned and crisp underneath, then flip and fry the other side.
Repeat with the rest and serve hot with rice and ketchup.

tips: No need to add salt; corned beef has plenty. A small diced boiled potato in the mix makes the patties go further.

title: Tortang sardinas
intro: Canned sardines mashed with egg, onion and garlic and fried into soft, savory patties. A budget ulam that turns two cans into dinner for four.

steps.text: Mash the drained sardines in a bowl, bones and all, with a fork.
Add the eggs, onion, garlic, flour, green onions and pepper and mix well.
Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Scoop in about 1/4 cup of the mixture per patty and flatten slightly.
Fry until golden underneath, then flip and fry the other side. Repeat with the rest.
Serve hot with rice; the tomato sauce from the can, warmed, makes a good drizzle.

tips: Taste a small fried spoonful first; sardine brands vary in saltiness, so add a pinch of salt only if it needs it.

title: Tortang upo
intro: Grated bottle gourd salted and squeezed, then mixed with egg and fried into tender patties. Light and mildly sweet, with crisp edges.

steps.text: Grate the upo on the coarse side of a grater. Toss with the salt and let stand.
Squeeze the upo by the handful to remove as much liquid as you can.
Beat the eggs in a bowl and whisk in the flour and pepper. Stir in the upo, onion and garlic.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Spoon in about 3 tablespoons of the mixture per patty and flatten.
Fry until golden underneath, then flip and fry the other side. Repeat with the rest.
Taste one and sprinkle with a little salt if needed. Serve with rice and banana ketchup.

tips: Ground pork, browned and cooled, can be stirred into the batter for a meatier version.

title: Tortang kalabasa
intro: Grated squash mixed with egg, flour and onion and fried into thin, crisp-edged fritters. Sweet and savory, good with rice or on their own with vinegar.

items.name: kalabasa (squash)
items.note: peeled and coarsely grated, about 2 cups

steps.text: Beat the eggs in a bowl and whisk in the flour, salt and pepper. Add a tablespoon or two of water if the batter is too stiff to coat the squash.
Stir in the grated squash, onion and green onions.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Spoon in about 3 tablespoons of the mixture per fritter and spread it thin.
Fry until golden and crisp underneath, then flip and fry the other side until the squash is cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and repeat with the rest. Serve hot with rice, ketchup or vinegar.

tips: Grate the squash on the coarse side; fine shreds turn mushy and the fritters lose their crisp edges.

title: Tortang malunggay
intro: A thick omelet packed with malunggay leaves, onion and tomato. Soft, lightly grassy and ready in minutes for breakfast or a quick ulam.

steps.text: Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper, then stir in the malunggay, onion and tomato.
Heat the oil in a 25 cm nonstick pan over medium heat. Pour in the egg mixture and spread the leaves evenly.
Lower the heat, cover and cook until the bottom is golden and the top is almost set.
Slide the torta onto a plate, flip it back into the pan and cook the other side.
Cut into wedges and serve with rice and ketchup.

tips: Strip the leaves just before using; malunggay leaves wilt and drop off the stems within a day.

title: Tortang togue
intro: Bean sprouts and carrot strips quickly sautéed, then set in egg and fried into crunchy patties. Juicy and savory, with soy-vinegar dip on the side.

steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a pan over high heat. Toss the garlic, onion, carrot and togue just until the sprouts start to wilt. Spread on a plate to cool.
Beat the eggs in a bowl and whisk in the flour, salt and pepper. Stir in the cooled vegetables.
Heat the remaining oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Scoop in about 1/3 cup of the mixture per patty and flatten.
Fry until golden underneath, then flip and fry the other side. Repeat with the rest.
Serve hot with rice and a dip of soy sauce and vinegar.

tips: Drain off any liquid the sprouts release before mixing them into the egg, or the patties will be soggy.

title: Tortang mais
intro: Sweet corn kernels held together with egg and a little flour and fried into crisp, lacy fritters. Sweet and salty, eaten with rice or as merienda with vinegar.

items.name: corn kernels
items.note: from 3 ears, or canned and well drained

steps.text: Beat the eggs in a bowl and whisk in the flour, cornstarch, salt and pepper until smooth.
Stir in the corn, onion and green onions. The batter should just coat the kernels.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Spoon in about 2 tablespoons of the mixture per fritter and spread thin.
Fry until golden and crisp underneath, then flip and fry the other side.
Drain on paper towels and repeat with the rest. Serve hot with vinegar or banana ketchup.

tips: Pat canned corn dry with a towel before mixing; wet kernels make the oil spit and the fritters soft.

title: Tortang hipon
intro: Chopped shrimp, onion and tomato folded into egg and fried into thick, juicy patties. Sweet from the shrimp and very good with rice and ketchup.

steps.text: Beat the eggs in a bowl with the flour, salt and pepper until smooth.
Stir in the shrimp, onion, garlic, tomato and green onions.
Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Scoop in about 1/4 cup of the mixture per patty and flatten slightly.
Fry until golden underneath and the shrimp turn pink, then flip and fry the other side. Repeat with the rest.
Serve hot with rice and ketchup.

tips: Chop the shrimp into pea-sized pieces so they cook through in the same time the egg takes to set.
